Killed-virus vaccines have suffered from FUD because detailed Phase 3 trial results haven't been published. Why they haven't is a bit mysterious. Turkey, UAE, and Brazil have completed randomized blinded control trials and announced good top-line results, but without details.

By good, we mean 50-79% for all cases (Brazil), ~90% for severe cases (Turkey) and "nearly complete" protection from death (Brazil). The US media pushes the dea that this old tech is unimpressive, but these results are similar to AZ's high-tech Ad vaccine:
https://t.co/0xSUGgDwp4

Today's news comes from CNN, hidden in an article about India's second wave. 

The result is that Bharat's killed virus vaccine (Covaxin) has had a similar % of breakthrough infections compared to the AZ vaccine (called Covishield there), 0.04% vs 0.03%:

https://t.co/Hf81hJzPAQ

These findings are easy to overlook, because the article is not about the vaccines per se, but just about refuting various myths arising from not examining the entire statistical dataset. The article doesn't even identify Covaxin and Covishield as killed-virus and Ad vaccines.

But the results are *very* interesting and informative, for four reasons:
1. They are from the real world.
2. They are from a very large population (1.7M and 15M people), so the effects of stochasticity are minimized.
3. The vaccines are similar: 2 doses, refrigeration-only

4. Both vaccine groups are in the same country and the vast majority of cases occurred at the same time (in the last month).

Thus we can compare, in a similar patient population, between a killed-virus vaccine and the "modern" AZ Ad vax that has reported detailed Ph3 results.

So now we can say with pretty high confidence that old-school killed-virus vaccines can have as high efficacy as newfangled adenovirus vaccines. This is completely consistent with what was previously reported for killed-virus vaccines.

And while Ad vax adverse reactions of VITT are exceedingly rare, there are no reported adverse reactions to killed-virus vax so far.
